## Summary

This assignment is hands-on practice for Milestone 2:
build a Docker [image]{.term tabindex="0" data-tip="A Docker image is a saved snapshot of a computer setup: an operating system, software and packages, ready to run. A container is one running copy of an image. You write the recipe for the image in a Dockerfile."} from a `Dockerfile`, and publish it to Docker Hub with GitHub Actions.

- [ ] Make a small uv (Python) **or** renv (R) project with two pinned packages
- [ ] Write a `Dockerfile` that installs them, and test it on your computer
- [ ] Publish the image to Docker Hub with a GitHub Actions workflow

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Readings for this assignment

-   [uv: pinning exact versions](https://ubc-dsci.github.io/reproducible-and-trustworthy-workflows-for-data-science/lectures/virtual-environments-python-uv-exact-pins.html)
    or [renv: declaring packages in `DESCRIPTION`](https://ubc-dsci.github.io/reproducible-and-trustworthy-workflows-for-data-science/lectures/virtual-environments-r-renv-description.html)
-   [Python packages with uv in an image](https://ubc-dsci.github.io/reproducible-and-trustworthy-workflows-for-data-science/lectures/containers-uv.html)
    or [R packages with renv in an image](https://ubc-dsci.github.io/reproducible-and-trustworthy-workflows-for-data-science/lectures/containers-renv.html)
-   [Building images for several platforms](https://ubc-dsci.github.io/reproducible-and-trustworthy-workflows-for-data-science/lectures/containers-platforms.html): the workflow in step 5
-   uv refresher: [DSCI 521 uv lecture notes](https://ubc-mds.github.io/DSCI_521_platforms-dsci_book/lectures/virtual-environments-uv.html)
:::

## Instructions

1.  **Make the repository.**
    Create a **public** GitHub.com repository under your personal account, named `dsci522-dockerfile-practice`,
    with a `README`. Clone it; everything below happens in this folder.

2.  **Make a small project** with uv **or** renv, whichever you prefer.
    It needs at least **two** packages you haven't used before, each **[pinned to an exact version]{.term tabindex="0" data-tip="Pinning means recording one exact version of a package (e.g. pandas==2.2.3), instead of whatever is newest. Everyone who installs your project then gets the same version, so the code behaves the same."}**.

    -   **uv:** `pyproject.toml` lists each package with `==`, and Python 3.11 or newer is pinned in `.python-version`.
        Commit `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock` and `.python-version`, but not `.venv/`.
    -   **renv:** `DESCRIPTION` lists each package with `(== x.y.z)`, using explicit snapshots.
        Commit `DESCRIPTION`, `renv.lock`, `.Rprofile` and `renv/`
        (the `.gitignore` inside `renv/` keeps the installed packages out).

3.  **Write a `Dockerfile`** in the root of your repository that installs your packages exactly as your [lock file]{.term tabindex="0" data-tip="A lock file (uv.lock for uv, renv.lock for renv) is generated by your environment manager. It records the exact version of every package your project uses, including the packages they depend on, so the environment can be rebuilt exactly."} records them
    (follow the uv or renv chapter in the readings). It should:

    -   start `FROM` a [base image]{.term tabindex="0" data-tip="The base image is the existing image your Dockerfile starts from, on the FROM line (e.g. rocker/r-ver:4.6.2 already has R installed). Your Dockerfile then adds your own packages on top."} with a version tag (for example `rocker/r-ver:4.6.2`), **not** `latest`
    -   `COPY` your project files, including the lock file, into the image
    -   `RUN` the command that installs the packages from the lock file

4.  **Test it on your computer.**
    Build the image, run a container from it, and load each package inside it.
    Fix problems now: debugging on your computer is much faster than on GitHub Actions.

5.  **Publish with GitHub Actions.**
    Set up Docker Hub and the secrets (see below), then copy the **single-platform** workflow from
    [Building images for several platforms](https://ubc-dsci.github.io/reproducible-and-trustworthy-workflows-for-data-science/lectures/containers-platforms.html)
    into `.github/workflows/publish-dockerhub.yml`.
    Change only its `IMAGE` line, to `<your-docker-hub-username>/dsci522-dockerfile-practice`, all in lowercase.

    The workflow pushes the image tagged `latest` and with the commit SHA.
    It runs when a push changes the `Dockerfile` or a lock file.
    To run it by hand: **Actions** tab \> the workflow \> **Run workflow**.

6.  **Check that it worked.**
    The run on the **Actions** tab finishes with a green check mark,
    and the image shows up in your Docker Hub repository.

7.  **Credit the workflow.**
    Add a `LICENSE.md` with the text of docker-uv-renv's [`LICENSE`](https://github.com/chendaniely/docker-uv-renv/blob/main/LICENSE) (MIT),
    plus a note that it only covers the code you copied (`.github/workflows/publish-dockerhub.yml`).

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Setting up Docker Hub and the GitHub secrets

1.  Create a free [Docker Hub](https://hub.docker.com/) account if you don't have one.
2.  Create a **public** Docker Hub repository named `dsci522-dockerfile-practice`.
3.  Create a Docker Hub [access token](https://docs.docker.com/security/access-tokens/) with Read & Write permissions.
    Copy it somewhere safe: you can only see it once.
4.  In your GitHub repository, add two
    [repository secrets](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-what-workflows-do/use-secrets)
    (Settings \> Secrets and variables \> Actions \> New repository secret),
    with exactly these names, because the workflow looks for them:
    -   `DOCKER_USERNAME`: your Docker Hub username
    -   `DOCKER_PASSWORD`: the access token (**not** your Docker Hub password)
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Troubleshooting

-   **Git refuses to push the workflow file:** your personal access token needs the **workflow** scope.
    On GitHub, go to Settings \> Developer settings \> Personal access tokens, select your token, and tick **workflow**.
-   **The workflow didn't start:** it only starts on its own when a push changes the `Dockerfile` or a lock file.
    Run it by hand from the **Actions** tab.
-   **The login step fails:** check the secret names, and that `DOCKER_PASSWORD` is an access token with Read & Write permissions.
:::

2.  your image on Docker Hub, in a repository named `dsci522-dockerfile-practice`

| -15%  | A package in `pyproject.toml` or `DESCRIPTION` is not pinned to an exact version |
| -15%  | There were authentication issues with publishing to Docker Hub |
| -33%  | Fewer than two packages are listed in `pyproject.toml` or `DESCRIPTION` |
